statement: The 2021 NDC describes the Kyrgyz Republic as highly climate-vulnerable and reliant on climate-sensitive sectors; disasters, disease, infrastructure damage, and reduced water can threaten development, energy, and irrigation.
compact_statement: The 2021 NDC describes the Kyrgyz Republic as highly climate-vulnerable and reliant on climate-sensitive sectors; disasters, disease, infrastructure damage, and reduced water can threaten development, energy, and irrigation.

source_refs.locator: NDC summary, PDF p. 3.

uncertainty: National NDC framing, not a new impact assessment.

statement: The NDC says women and children in rural households carry much of the work of obtaining domestic water and fuel, while women face barriers to finance, training, technology, and climate decision-making.
compact_statement: The NDC says women and children in rural households carry much of the work of obtaining domestic water and fuel, while women face barriers to finance, training, technology, and climate decision-making.

source_refs.locator: Gender aspects of NDC implementation, PDF pp. 17-18.

uncertainty: This is the government's assessment; the cited section notes gaps in gender-disaggregated data.

statement: The NDC warns that inequitable access to natural and social resources amid climate pressures can lead to social conflict and calls for women's participation in resource allocation and conflict reduction.
compact_statement: The NDC warns that inequitable access to natural and social resources amid climate pressures can lead to social conflict and calls for women's participation in resource allocation and conflict reduction.
scenario: The NDC cites water-availability decline over 2050-2100; the conflict-risk statement does not specify an emissions scenario.

source_refs.locator: Gender aspects of NDC implementation and water-availability outlook, PDF p. 18.

uncertainty: Government-stated potential risk; not observed conflict attribution.

statement: The World Bank summary reports more severe storms, landslides, heat waves, and droughts; inaction could cut GDP 2–3% by 2040 via agriculture and infrastructure damage.
compact_statement: The World Bank summary reports more severe storms, landslides, heat waves, and droughts; inaction could cut GDP 2–3% by 2040 via agriculture and infrastructure damage.
scenario: Policy-inaction case; the summary does not identify its climate-model scenario.

source_refs.locator: Key findings, official CCDR summary page, paragraphs on hazards and cost of inaction (accessed 2026-10-26).

uncertainty: Summary page; full model details not inspected.

statement: The summary says inaction could push 170,000 more people into poverty by 2040, especially in rural areas, and reduce jobs and incomes for the bottom 20%.
compact_statement: The summary says inaction could push 170,000 more people into poverty by 2040, especially in rural areas, and reduce jobs and incomes for the bottom 20%.
scenario: Policy-inaction case; the summary does not specify the climate-model scenario.

source_refs.locator: Key findings, official CCDR summary page, paragraphs on poverty and distributional impacts (accessed 2026-10-26).

uncertainty: Modeled projections, not observed poverty outcomes.

statement: The summary estimates up to 24% of irrigation demand could go unmet by mid-century as temperatures and crop-water needs rise.
compact_statement: The summary estimates up to 24% of irrigation demand could go unmet by mid-century as temperatures and crop-water needs rise.
scenario: The official summary does not specify the climate-model scenario for this estimate.

source_refs.locator: Key findings, official CCDR summary page, paragraph on irrigation demand (accessed 2026-10-26).

uncertainty: Detailed assumptions are not shown on the summary page.

statement: The Resilient Landscape Restoration Project aims to benefit over 50,000 rural people, including women and vulnerable groups, across Jalal-Abad, Osh, Issyk-Kul, and Naryn regions.
compact_statement: The Resilient Landscape Restoration Project aims to benefit over 50,000 rural people, including women and vulnerable groups, across Jalal-Abad, Osh, Issyk-Kul, and Naryn regions.

source_refs.locator: Project coverage and intended beneficiaries, press-release paragraphs 121-126 (accessed 2026-10-26).

uncertainty: Beneficiary count is a project target, not an achieved result.

statement: The project plans to improve glacier, snow-cover, and mudflow monitoring and restore landscapes with local labor payments and livelihood training; implementation is planned through 2029.
compact_statement: The project plans to improve glacier, snow-cover, and mudflow monitoring and restore landscapes with local labor payments and livelihood training; implementation is planned through 2029.

source_refs.locator: Project activities and implementation period, press-release paragraphs 123-128 (accessed 2026-10-26).

uncertainty: These are proposed project activities, not verified implementation results.

statement: The Isfara supplies irrigation and city water to more than 40 villages in Batken district and downstream Isfara district in Tajikistan.
compact_statement: The Isfara supplies irrigation and city water to more than 40 villages in Batken district and downstream Isfara district in Tajikistan.
institutions: Small Basin Council of the Isfara River

source_refs.locator: PDF printed p. 5, Isfara River and research area

uncertainty: Describes river dependence, not household-level access or allocation volumes.

statement: In the 2019 six-village Isfara study, 72% perceived lower winter snowfall and 78% hotter summers; separate snow and upstream precipitation measurements were incomplete.
compact_statement: In the 2019 six-village Isfara study, 72% perceived lower winter snowfall and 78% hotter summers; separate snow and upstream precipitation measurements were incomplete.

source_refs.locator: Printed p.30 (one-based PDF p.31), perceptions of climate and resources.

uncertainty: Percentages are respondents' perceptions; the study notes incomplete snow and upstream precipitation observations.

statement: The 2019 Isfara study records perceived irrigation shortages and lower yields associated with erosion, pests and disease; perceived falling river water contrasted with an increasing measured runoff trend.
compact_statement: The 2019 Isfara study records perceived irrigation shortages and lower yields associated with erosion, pests and disease; perceived falling river water contrasted with an increasing measured runoff trend.
geographies: Isfara catchment villages in Batken Province

source_refs.locator: Printed p.31 (one-based PDF p.32), yield and runoff comparison.

uncertainty: Distinguishes perceived water shortage from the study's measured runoff trend; local demand may explain the difference.

statement: The 2020 Isfara research paper describes contested water, pasture and land redistribution and unclear borders as historical conflict drivers; this does not isolate a climate effect or describe the present border settlement.
compact_statement: The 2020 Isfara research paper describes contested water, pasture and land redistribution and unclear borders as historical conflict drivers; this does not isolate a climate effect or describe the present border settlement.

source_refs.locator: PDF printed pp. 4-5, resource competition and conflict context

statement: International Alert's 2021 analysis describes water disputes and agreement violations in the Batken-Sughd clashes, with climate, nationalism, politics and COVID-19 adding stress.
compact_statement: International Alert's 2021 analysis describes water disputes and agreement violations in the Batken-Sughd clashes, with climate, nationalism, politics and COVID-19 adding stress.

statement: The 2021 regional analysis describes restrictions on cross-border resource sharing and plans for reservoirs or canals without sufficient local consultation, warning of tension risks.
compact_statement: The 2021 regional analysis describes restrictions on cross-border resource sharing and plans for reservoirs or canals without sufficient local consultation, warning of tension risks.
